title: 1918 influenza pandemic
summary: The 1918 influenza pandemic, caused by an H1N1 virus with avian-origin genes, spread worldwide during 1918–1919. The CDC estimates about 500 million people, one-third of the world's population, were infected and at least 50 million died worldwide, about 675,000 in the United States; other accounts put deaths as high as 100 million. There is no universal consensus on where it began; in the United States it was first identified in military personnel in spring 1918.

uncertainty.note: CDC: spread worldwide during 1918-1919. The CDC EID article dates the first wave from March 1918 and a third wave in early 1919; HISTORY says the pandemic lasted two years from its outbreak in the U.S.

as_recorded.value: The first (spring) wave began in March 1918; third wave in early 1919

where.historical_name: Global; the CDC says there is not universal consensus on where the virus originated

importance.justification: The CDC calls it the most severe pandemic in recent history, with at least 50 million deaths worldwide.

reviewer_note: Planet-wide pin by design: no single origin site is sourced (CDC: no universal consensus; EID: 'its origin remains puzzling'). HISTORY states the disease was first recorded in Haskell County, Kansas, in January 1918 and that it lasted two years; the CDC does not support a single origin, so the pin was not set there. Death estimates: CDC at least 50 million; EID about 50 million, arguably as high as 100 million; HISTORY 50–100 million.
